note: What this decompressor asserts about the SPC7110 and where each assertion comes from. No manufacturer document for this part is known to exist, so nothing here is verified and the file says so for each constant rather than leaving a reader to infer it from the absence of quotes.

order: a manufacturer document, of which there is none
a recording taken off a real SPC7110, of which there is none on this machine
the reference implementation, which is where all of this comes from
authority.why: The SPC7110 was made for Nintendo and no datasheet was published. The algorithm was reconstructed from the silicon or from its output, so the top two rungs are both empty and the third is carrying the package.
authority.whatIsMissing: Any document naming this part. Searched on 2026-08-21; nothing was found, and nothing suggests one was ever published.

comparedAgainst.what: The reference decompressor, built from a commit and a set of extracts both pinned in conformance/pinned.json, asked to expand 200 streams of random bytes across all three modes: 102,400 bytes compared, none of them produced by this model.

modes.why: Three decompression modes, producing one, two and four bit planes.
modes.evidence: The reference implementation, corroborated by the cartridges that carry this chip using all three.
modes.howToSettleIt: A datasheet, or a die photograph of the mode decode.

contexts.why: How many probability contexts the arithmetic coder keeps.
contexts.howToSettleIt: A datasheet, or a die photograph of the context memory.

bufferBytes.why: The ring buffer the decompressor emits into before a caller reads from it.
bufferBytes.howToSettleIt: A die photograph, or a measurement showing where output wraps.
bufferBytes.note: Sixty four is also the size of an eight bit per dot character, and that is a coincidence rather than a derivation: this is an internal ring buffer and its size is not tied to any character format. It is written down because the coincidence is inviting and inviting is how a guess becomes a citation.

spanFull.why: The width of the coder's interval before any subdivision.

renormaliseBelow.why: The threshold below which the coder renormalises.

resetLine.value: nothing, because this part carries no state between decompressions
resetLine.evidence: Not a claim about a pin. Every decompression is started from its own header and its own context table, and nothing survives from one to the next, so there is no state a reset could clear. What the real part's reset pin does to its internal registers is not known and is not modelled.
resetLine.howToSettleIt: A capture of the cartridge bus across a console reset part-way through a decompression.

notStated: Everything. No manufacturer document for this part is known to exist, so nothing here is verified in the sense the sibling repositories use the word.
How the chip behaves on a malformed stream. Every implementation guesses and none of the guesses can be checked.
Anything about timing. How long a decode takes, and whether a console reading the output can outrun it, is unmodelled and unmeasured.
Whether the three modes are the only three, or the only three any cartridge used.
